prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Grid Dispatcher: requirements→Wildmere; priority safety>protection>export. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss, shutdown on confirmed fire; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System (safe blade position), Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Mode Turbine Lockout: no remote restart during fire investigation. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment; mode Substation Degraded. Alarms not cleared just because detector normal. Substation Operator switches only in active window with Control Engineer authorization; notifies Grid Dispatcher. Outages: Marine Coordinator checks vessel timing; Electrical Technician inspects after isolations; Work Permit Portal updated first; Duty Planner records times. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry/alarms→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room keeps last validated limit on comms loss. Operations Radio Console: voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft; Vessel Master read-back; Transfer Manifest Addendum from Duty Planner. Evacuation: Personnel Tracking Console; HSE Officer advises re-entry; Field Supervisor status→Shore Control Room. North/South Access Scanners: individual credential, active, belongs to presenter, current authorization for area/time; else deny, barrier stays closed (also if check incomplete); no override/bypass; local permit/deny indicator; no holding barrier; anti-tailgating at south; visitors same checks; escort verified; denial→Field Supervisor/HSE Officer. Logs every attempt (transaction ID, credential, time, point, outcome, rule), tamper-protected, for review. Pre-service and routine checks; faults→out of service; scanner unavailable→approved alternative process with named approver; credential-free emergency egress; change control. East Service Lift: door-interlock and overload check before accepting movement request; Field Supervisor coordinates pre-shift inspection (visual,

New part:
S866: The hoist, suspension points, and visible cable sections are examined for wear, corrosion, or abnormal movement.
S867: The Electrical Technician verifies that the lift supply and protective devices show no active fault indication.
S868: The inspector confirms that the rated capacity and operating instructions remain legible at the car entrance.
S869: The Field Supervisor records the inspection result and any observed defects in the maintenance system.
S870: A defect affecting safe operation prevents release until the required repair and verification are complete.
S871: The Work Permit Portal is checked for active restrictions that could conflict with lift operation.
S872: The Duty Planner confirms that the planned work can proceed within the lift capacity and operating limits.
S873: Personnel are briefed on the permitted landings, maximum occupancy, and emergency actions before boarding.
S874: The Personnel Tracking Console is used to maintain an accurate record of personnel entering and leaving the route.
S875: Equipment is inspected for dimensions, mass, and secure packaging before it is accepted for transport.
S876: The Storekeeper confirms that equipment intended for the lift is ready and properly identified for the work party.
S877: Long or unstable loads are not carried unless an approved handling arrangement keeps the load contained within the car.
S878: The operator positions each load to avoid obstructing doors, controls, and emergency access.
S879: The Field Supervisor confirms that no person is exposed to a suspended or shifting load during movement.
S880: The release decision is based on a satisfactory inspection, valid work authorization, and compliance with stated limits.
S881: The Field Supervisor communicates the release status to the work party and records the time that service is authorized.
S882: During operation, users report unusual noise, vibration, door behavior, or control response immediately.
S883: The lift is removed from service if a new condition could compromise safe movement, pending assessment and corrective action.
S884: The West Service Lift provides vertical access along the west route between the designated service landings.
S885: Its use is limited to personnel and equipment authorized for the turbine work area.
S886: Before boarding, the Field Supervisor confirms that the work authorization covers the intended landing and task.
S887: The Field Supervisor also verifies that the landing is accessible and that the route is clear of obstructions.
S888: The operator checks the lift identification, rated capacity, and current service status before each operating period.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
